title: A phase runs its ready tasks as waves, and task scopes carry their companions
description: F600 (high) and F599 (med) from the danuvia testbed. Design, prior art, roles and decisions: quality-gates-internal plans/2026-10-09-f600-f599-waves-design.md (D1 unset width = 1 and init writes auto; D3 re-gate only on path overlap; D7 the plan-gate binding is agent-written).
desiredOutcome: A phase runs its ready disjoint tasks concurrently, each gated in its own worktree and integrated serially onto the phase tree with conflicting or undeclared overlaps refused by name, width 1 reproduces 3.2.0 exactly, and a task's scope carries the dependency, locale and runner-config files its change cannot avoid.

findings.issue: In a wave a per-task reviewer (review.perTask always, or signals when a signal fires) is dispatched after the gate and BEFORE the task's bytes are integrated. Its brief's diff is `git diff HEAD -- <files>` read from the phase tree, where the task's change does not exist yet (it lives in the task tree until integrate-task runs), and the reviewer brief carries no tree:/base: lines (wave_tree_lines feeds the executor brief only). The reviewer is shown an empty diff and answers intent/inherited-tests about nothing. Default `phase` mode is unaffected. No case runs a wave with per_task other than phase (_wave_repo takes per_task but every wave case uses the default).
findings.resolution: fixed in P124.15-k2x (a7b5de217b55): Either point the reviewer brief at the task's tree (tree:, base:, and a diff read with `git -C <tree> diff <base>` plus untracked files) and say so in audit-reviewer.md, or integrate before the reviewer is due. Add a wave case with per_task=always asserting the reviewer brief's diff is non-empty.

findings.issue: take_stamp passes `--project <task tree> --manifest <phase tree manifest>`. stamp-verification's recorder_exclusion labels a manifest outside the project root by its ABSOLUTE path, so every wave executor stamp stores `"manifest": "<absolute machine path>/docs/audit/audit-plan.json"` (reproduced against a scratch repo plus linked worktree: the stamp and the content note both carry the absolute path, and the note reports every recorder path as 'could not be left out'). file-return writes that text verbatim into the committed executor return with no scrub, so a wave run commits a machine path into evidence: the class P122 removed, and what tools/check-committed-pii.py exists to refuse. Serial runs are unaffected (manifest inside the root, label is relative). wv4 only asserts the return was filed.
findings.resolution: fixed in P124.14-k2x (3d6156a580f8): Give take a way to store the project-relative label of the phase tree's manifest when the measured tree is a task tree (or compute the label against the phase tree and pass the tree only as the digest root), and add a wave case asserting the filed stamp's manifest field is relative and the return holds no absolute path.

findings.issue: Tree creation is not resumable, which the design promised ('worktrees are found again through their markers'). (a) task-add writes the marker, then runs executor.worktreeSetup (an install, minutes) before returning; a session death or Ctrl-C in that window leaves a marked tree that the driver state does not name. The rerun calls task-add, which refuses 'task X already has a tree', so the run stops and only a manual task-remove recovers it. (b) On a failed setup add_tree records the tree in wave.trees and stops; the next `next` finds the tree recorded and dispatches the executor straight into the half-provisioned tree, never re-running setup, so the 'could not run, no attempt spent' promise turns into a red gate and a spent attempt. (c) close_wave drops wave.trees while a blocked member's tree is kept on disk; unblocking that task into a later wave hits the same 'already has a tree' refusal. All three are loud, none loses bytes. The wc cases crash only after integration.
findings.resolution: fixed in P124.15-k2x (a7b5de217b55): In add_tree treat the 'already has a tree' refusal for a tree whose marker base equals the wave base as adoption (record it, and re-run setup unless a setup-ok mark is stored), keep an unresolved setup failure in the member's state so the next step retries it, and carry kept trees of blocked members across close_wave. Add a case that kills the driver between task-add and the state write, and one for a failed setup followed by a second next.

findings.issue: The only thing that keeps a discarded undeclared change from being destroyed is tree_holds_only_integrated deciding the tree still holds bytes the phase tree lacks, because retire_member then removes clean trees with `task-remove --force` (which also deletes ignored files). Mutation on a scratch copy: making the comparison never report a difference (`if sides[0] != sides[1]` to `if False`) leaves wv, wr, wc, w1, wz and pf stages all passing. No case answers `discard` and checks the tree survives and is named, so the guard can be deleted without a test failing. By reading, the guard is correct (a path present in the tree and absent from the phase tree compares unequal).
findings.resolution: fixed in P124.15-k2x (a7b5de217b55): Add a wave case: P1.2 writes an undeclared notes.txt, answer discard, close; assert the task closes, notes.txt is absent from the phase tree, the tree directory still exists with notes.txt in it, and the did-line says 'kept'.

findings.issue: Design D2 offers `redo|block` for a conflict and says redo does not spend an attempt; the code offers `retry|block` for every integration refusal kind (dirty, non-mergeable, conflict), recuts the tree with --force and spends an attempt. For a dirty phase tree the work is fine and only the tree needs cleaning, yet the only non-block answer discards a green executor run.
findings.resolution: Offer a re-integrate answer for `dirty`, and make the conflict redo not count against maxAttempts, or record the deviation.

findings.issue: close_wave moves every tree still standing into state.keptTrees, including a done member's tree kept because it holds a discarded undeclared change. Only a later task-add for that same task pops the entry, and a done task is never re-added, so the entry stays in the driver state for the life of the phase and is named once, in the wave-closing print. Nothing later lists a kept tree for a human to clean up.
findings.resolution: Name keptTrees again in the sign-off hand-off or in /audit:doctor, or record the path on the task's journal row, so a discarded change's tree is findable after the print scrolls away.
